origin.description: Adds a theoretical Lorenz curve to an existing plot.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Parameter vector for the distribution. Leave it NULL when the parameters are already fixed inside x.

arguments.name: lwd, col, ...
arguments.text: Line width, color, and further arguments passed to lines. The default color is the second palette entry.

origin.details: The curve is evaluated on (0:1000) * 0.001 and added with lines. No diagonal is drawn. The usual use is to lay a fitted distribution over an empirical Lorenz curve.

translation.description: Adds a theoretical Lorenz curve to the current axes.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.text: A theoretical Lorenz curve callable, with the same calling rule as plot_theor_lc.

arguments.name: parameter
arguments.text: Passed as parameter= to fn. None calls fn(grid) alone.

arguments.name: color
arguments.text: Line color. The default C1 is Matplotlib's second cycle color, in place of R's col=2.

arguments.name: ax
arguments.text: Axes to draw on. None uses the current axes.

translation.details: Same 1001-point grid as plot_theor_lc. Only the curve is added, in a color that stays distinct from a black empirical curve.
translation.value: A dict with p equal to the grid and y equal to the ordinates.
translation.example:
from ineq.lorenz import Lc
from ineq.plots import lines_theor_lc, plot_lc
from ineq.theor import lc_lognorm

x = [541, 1463, 2445, 3438, 4437, 5401, 6392, 8304, 11904, 22261]
n = [482, 825, 722, 690, 661, 760, 745, 2140, 1911, 1024]
plot_lc(Lc(x, n=n))
lines_theor_lc(lc_lognorm, parameter=0.78)
